column1: # Reviewed upstream backports -- see scripts/thin-fork-guard.sh's header
# comment ("Reviewed upstream backport" section) for the full design and
# verify_reviewed_backport()'s exact 7-point runtime verification.
# This is NOT a path allowlist, a permanent per-file exemption, or a way to
# approve a range of commits. Each record authorizes exactly one reviewed
# file state, derived from exactly one named, already-accepted official
# CrossPoint commit, applied to one exact recorded base blob. One extra
# Midad-authored line, the wrong upstream SHA, or a target commit that also
# touches unrelated content each cause the record to stop matching.
# This file is a SECURITY_BOUNDARY_FILES entry (see thin-fork-guard.sh) --
# an ordinary PR cannot modify it. Changing it requires the same human
# security-boundary maintenance procedure as thin-fork-guard.sh itself
# (docs/upstream-sync-architecture.md's "Security-boundary file maintenance"
# section).
# Format: TSV, one record per line.
#   PATH<TAB>UPSTREAM_COMMIT_SHA<TAB>BASE_BLOB_SHA<TAB>APPROVED_HEAD_BLOB_SHA<TAB>NOTE
# BASE_BLOB_SHA is the EFFECTIVE base for that path: the path's adopted-
# upstream blob (see find_adopted_upstream_blob) when this PR's own history
# contains a qualifying real merge for it, otherwise BASE_REF's own blob.
# src/activities/reader/TxtReaderActivity.cpp: PR #149 (phase2/reader-
# dictionary-convergence) real-merged CrossPoint through commit 080b1d71
# (adopted baseline blob 55dea5bea040c7f5ee4d734590d82cb09d01860f, verified
# identical back to 33f07db7 -- upstream never touched this file in
# between). CrossPoint later added an unrelated x4pro/papermono commit
# (bbca4886, intentionally deferred out of Phase 2) and then, on top of
# that, accepted Midad's own independently-authored skipPages() end-of-book
# clamp fix as CrossPoint PR #3061 (commit 63fcbab0). This record authorizes
# exactly that isolated fix, applied to the adopted baseline, independent of
# bbca4886's unrelated changes to the same file -- see
# scripts/test-thin-fork-guard.sh's regression test for this exact scenario
# (an unrelated upstream commit touching the same file before the accepted
# fix must not block the narrow backport, and must not smuggle its own
# changes in).
